reviews.title: My files were within limits and the limits decreased over time. Now they are threatening to delete.
reviews.text:
I put a bunch of family photos into Dropbox because I had to move and most of my property was destroyed. I am using free, but can’t afford to upgrade now until things better. They’ve been sending me emails that have repeatedly told me to get more storage, then it started talking about being over the limit for multiple emails. About a year later they are now sending me threatening emails about deleting EVERYTHING and claiming it’s because either more was added, I had a paid tier or I was part of a team. None of these things are true and I’ve added nothing. 
What little I have left to remember sentimental moments is what they are threatening to delete to pressure me into upgrading. I want to upgrade, I find this service extremely useful and up until recently trustworthy… but these threats have really made me want to just stop using this service altogether. 
I don’t appreciate these emails I can’t reply to “do not reply” but they are telling me they’ll delete everything without elaborating on if I can decrease some of the files or what options I have. 
So I plan to try and find an alternative storage until I can afford to either print out everything or subscribe. 
Sick of these emails, probably won’t use Dropbox anymore.

reviews.title: Title: 12+ Years as a Customer — Now I Can’t Access My Own Files Without Paying!
reviews.text:
Rating: 1 Star

I have had a Dropbox account for over 12 years, dating back to when my children were in elementary school. I have not added new files in years, yet suddenly Dropbox began notifying me that I had exceeded my storage limit and needed to purchase a monthly subscription.

I have not changed how I use this account, so why is this suddenly happening?

In an attempt to resolve the issue, I even deleted files that I wanted to keep. Unfortunately, that did not solve anything.

Now I cannot access my own files without being prompted to pay for additional storage. These are personal files and memories that I have trusted Dropbox to store for over a decade.

I have submitted a support request, received a ticket number, and still have not received a meaningful response. There is no accessible telephone support for customers like me, leaving me with absolutely no way to speak directly with someone about this issue.

I have screenshots documenting everything.

I am extremely disappointed in Dropbox’s customer service and the way this situation has been handled. After more than a decade of using this service, I should not have to fight to access my own files.

I am requesting three simple things:

1. Restore access to my existing files so I can download them.
2. Explain why my storage limit suddenly became an issue when I have not been adding files.
3. Have an actual customer service representative respond to my existing support ticket.

I do not want to purchase a monthly su

I still like the original idea, but it’s not worth the cost to me anymore.

I send approximately 40 audio links to clients each month, and many of them complain that they don't know how to preview or download the file. On mobile, the “Open in browser” option is shown in very small text, while the much larger “Open in app” button makes recipients believe they must install the Dropbox app before they can access the file.

I find this design misleading and unfair to users. I regularly have to explain to clients how to open the link without installing the app, which is frustrating, embarrassing, and makes my service appear less professional.

This screen could be skipped altogether and the user should be taken directly to the file

reviews.title: nope - this isn’t it
reviews.text:
Considering the money I’ve spent over the last 10 plus years, it’s far too frustrating to see the minor issues (which are annoying and obvious m) be overlooked for new elements that feel pointless and unnecessary.

Yes, I wrote my problems on the forums, yes I spoke to help desk. “maybe that’ll be implemented in the future” was the answer. That was 5 years ago.

Alphabetically listing my  folders in the app isn’t a revolutionary concept - but for dropbox it’s been a dexade in the making… maybe next year perhaps?… a boy can dream 🙄

Now I write because as well as the above, now the app won’t show new “recent” FILES: when I pull down to refresh on app, the wheel stays frozen forever.

Suffice to say, this isn’t really good enough considering the £1000’s  i’ve spent for you to just host my 5gb of files.

I would recommend google drive over this - and maybe wetransfer. Dropbox seem complacent and expensive to me tbh.

reviews.text: I’ve been using Dropbox for many years and I always seem to have issues with their products. They have absolutely terrible customer service…amongst the worst I’ve ever experienced. reviews.title: Dropbox Backup (not)
reviews.text:
Dropbox Backup fails the single most important test of a backup: can you actually restore all your data?
In my case:
•Backup completed successfully.
•Files were visible in Dropbox Backup.
•There was no viable way to restore the full dataset.
•Large downloads fail due to size/file-count limits that are not clearly disclosed.
•Attempting smaller downloads revealed that many original files (JPEGs) were simply not downloadable.
•Support provided contradictory and ultimately dismissive responses.

This is not a user error or edge case — large photo libraries are normal. Dropbox Backup behaves more like a snapshot viewer than a real backup system.

If you care about actually getting your data back, use Time Machine, Backblaze, Arq, CCC, etc. Dropbox Backup is not in the same category.

reviews.title: The worst cloud experience I’ve ever had. DO NOT USE FOR PROFESSIONAL VIDEOGRAPHERS
reviews.text:
I run a video production company and our entire workflow relies on sending files and deliverables to clients. I switched to Dropbox thinking it would be reliable for transferring large video projects. Instead, it’s been a complete nightmare. I will making long form and social medias about this nightmare so that everyone in the video production industry avoids them. 

Dropbox started blocking every single link I sent to clients, preventing them from downloading files, reviewing cuts, or accessing final deliverables. Their system claimed I had exceeded over 1TB of bandwidth, which makes absolutely no sense. I had less than 15GB of actual downloads during that time period. I track all project file transfers internally, so I know for a fact that number is impossible.

When I contacted support, I expected some sort of transparency. Instead, they told me they “can’t show bandwidth usage for privacy reasons” EVEN THOUGH IM THE PLAYING CUSTOMER ASKING FOR DATA ON MY OWN ACCOUNT. How does it violate privacy to tell ME how much data MY account has used? ESPECIALLY WHEN I KNOW FOR A FACT I WAS NO WHERE CLOSE TO THE BANDWIDTH.

So for weeks, client delivery links broke randomly. I looked unprofessional, & deadlines were delayed. Meanwhile Dropbox’s only solution was essentially: Wait until the limit resets and hope it doesn’t happen again.

If you’re a creative, videographer, filmmaker, or agency that sends large files: Do NOT rely on Dropbox.
